blocks.text: Known 55+ manufactured-home parks and co-ops: what the sources show

These are the 55+ places named in public sources where you can own the home. Pad rent, shares and fees quoted below are listing-stated for one home on one date, not a park tariff, so confirm them with the park.
Alouette Retirement Mobile Home Park — 12868 229 St (East Central)

A 55+ manufactured home park in the residential streets east of downtown. A current listing states "55 PLUS age restriction — Alouette Retirement Mobile Home Park," with listing-stated terms: pad rental fee $713.31, city taxes $457.37, metered water billed quarterly, no dogs, indoor cat only, 2 residents per unit, and "no financing permitted in this community." All figures and rules are listing-stated — confirm against the park's tenancy agreement and park rules before relying on them.
Val Maria — 21163 Lougheed Hwy (Southwest Maple Ridge)

A manufactured-home park on the Lougheed Highway corridor; current listing text for homes in the park states "VAL MARIA, 55+ age restricted manufactured home park," with a listing-stated monthly pad rent of $850 and 2 small pets allowed. The address carries multiple units in the topic feed. Listing-stated — confirm the age rule, pad rent and pet rules against the park's tenancy agreement and park rules.
Rules that affect 55+ park homes

items.t: Manufactured-home parks run on tenancy law, not strata law: Pad tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and its Regulation (B.C. Reg. 481/2003), not the Strata Property Act — so the strata age-bylaw machinery (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, Regulation 7.01 exemptions) does not apply inside a park. A home owner must provide a purchaser with the written tenancy agreement and the written park rules, and a sale is an assignment of the pad tenancy that requires the park owner's consent.

A park's 55+ rule has its own legal footing: The MHPTA assignment rules expressly recognise a park where every pad is reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 (or 2+ tenants, at least one of whom has reached 55), as set out in s. 10(2)(b)(i) of the Human Rights Code — the park owner can refuse an assignment where no purchaser meets that age requirement. That is how Alouette's and Val Maria's 55+ rules operate: through park rules and assignment consent, not through a strata bylaw.

For contrast — the strata rule that does not apply here: only 55+ age bylaws are legal in BC strata now (Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1 and 123.2; sub-55 bylaws invalid since Nov 24, 2022), and strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since the same date. A park can still set its own occupancy and rental rules in its park rules — do not import strata assumptions into a park purchase.
City zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, s. 626, Zone RMH (Manufactured Home Park Residential): is the dedicated zone for this housing form in Maple Ridge.
Tenure paperwork is the diligence core of a park purchase

The registry covers both manufactured and modular homes: The Province's manufactured-home registry covers both forms, which is why this page in practice covers manufactured and modular product together.

Floodplain: the City's floodplain framework (flood construction level 6.7 m geodetic including freeboard along the river flats; Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibiting rental accommodation/suites on floodplain properties) is per-lot diligence for any park or owned-land manufactured home at the city's south/west lowland edges.
Property taxes / deferment: Note the Alouette listing separately itemises "city taxes" on top of pad rent — who pays what on a pad is set by the tenancy agreement, not by strata practice.

blocks.text: Good to know before you buy a park home

items.t: The two 55+ entries in rest on current MLS listing text that names the park and states its age rule — solid enough to print as listing-stated, not a substitute for the park's own rules document.

The city's zoning has a park-specific zone. Zone RMH, Manufactured Home Park Residential (Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, s. 626) is a dedicated zone for this housing form — a park's zoning, not just its rules, is part of its long-term security.

The two parks sit at opposite ends of the core. Alouette (229 St) is in the East Central residential streets beside the Fraserview 55+ cluster; Val Maria (21163 Lougheed Hwy) is on the highway corridor in Southwest Maple Ridge — a "Maple Ridge 55+ park" search is really two different neighbourhood decisions.

"No financing permitted" is a park rule, not a lender decision. Alouette's listing states it outright — in park product, the park's own rules can close the financing question before any bank is asked.

Scope and area context

items.t: This is a city-wide topic, not a neighbourhood: manufactured (mobile) homes for sale across the City of Maple Ridge — principally homes on rented pads in manufactured home parks, plus manufactured and modular homes on owned land.
Municipal zoning carries a dedicated zone for this housing form: Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 includes s. 626, Zone RMH, Manufactured Home Park Residential.
Schools: Maple Ridge is School District 42 (Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows).

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Mobile Homes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Maple Ridge's manufactured homes sit in seven park sites across the city, not in one district. A City report counts approximately 205 manufactured homes in home park sites, and says all seven sites would require rezoning before any redevelopment.

The southwest of the city, including Hammond, is bounded by Pitt Meadows and the Katzie First Nation to the west and by the Fraser River to the south, and Wharf Street in Hammond serves as both a road and a dike.
Lougheed Highway is the main east–west corridor through the park areas, and it carries the R3 RapidBus between Coquitlam Central Station and Haney Place.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Mobile Homes: the housing stock

items.t: The standard form here is a rented pad in a manufactured home park, and one co-operative that is often confused with a park. 7600-2019.
Alouette Retirement Manufactured Home Park, 12868 229 Street in East Central Maple Ridge, is a pad-rental park; an age-55-plus rule is stated only in listing sources.
Val Maria, 21163 Lougheed Highway in Southwest Maple Ridge, is a leasehold non-strata pad-rental park.

The Maples Housing Co-operative, 21570 Cherrington Avenue, is a housing co-operative of 31 semi-detached co-op homes, not a manufactured-home park, and is included only so buyers do not mix the two tenure forms up.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Mobile Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Maple Ridge's Manufactured Home Park Redevelopment Tenant Assistance Policy No. 6.27, in an updated version effective July 28, 2026, applies where residents are expected to be displaced if the City approves a development application, and it supplements the MHPTA.
Policy 6.27 works alongside the City's Tenant Protection Bylaw No. 8106-2026, Policy 6.32 Tenant Relocation Assistance, and Policy 6.40 Rental Protection.

Assigning a pad tenancy to a buyer needs the park owner's prior written consent on Residential Tenancy Branch (RTB) Form 10; the owner must respond so the home owner receives it by the 10th day, and no response by the end of day 10 means consent is deemed given.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Mobile Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The whole city has only about 205 manufactured homes in parks, so this is a small resale stock rather than a deep market.
Policy 6.27 was replaced by an updated version effective July 28, 2026 that supersedes the September 26, 2023 version, and it is scheduled for review on July 28, 2028.

The City's tenant protection page groups the park policy with a Tenant Protection Bylaw, a Tenant Relocation Assistance policy, and a Rental Protection policy, so park residents sit inside a wider city tenant-protection system.

From January 1, 2026, metered water and sewer in Maple Ridge moved to seasonal metered rates, and the sewer flat fee no longer appears on the tax notice for metered customers, while flat-rate customers are still billed water and sewer on the tax notice.
The City monitors the North and South Alouette Rivers, Kanaka Creek, and the Fraser River, publishes flood maps, and treats the April-to-July freshet as the main flood season.

School District 42 (Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows) serves the city, and the provincial school list for the district includes Alouette Elementary at 22155 Isaac Crescent and Maple Ridge Elementary at 20820 River Road.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Mobile Homes: development and new projects

items.t: The active municipal work is policy, not a named park application: the City updated Policy No. 6.27 effective July 28, 2026, covering communication, relocation planning, compensation, moving help, right to return when possible, and replacement housing for displaced park residents.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Mobile Homes: getting around

items.t: TransLink runs transit in Maple Ridge, and its R3 Lougheed Highway RapidBus runs between Coquitlam Central Station and Haney Place with service at least every 10 minutes at peak times and every 15 minutes off-peak, from 6 a.m. to midnight.
TransLink's Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows area planning documents include a combined map for local routes 743 and 744, which are the local buses serving the Haney and Hammond sides of the city.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Mobile Homes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood is the first check: a manufactured home must meet the same Flood Construction Level as any other residence under Bylaw No. 8121-2026, so a buyer should confirm the pad's flood status before removing subjects.

Redevelopment risk runs through City Hall: because every park site needs rezoning to redevelop, a rezoning application is the early-warning sign, and Policy 6.27 is the document that sets out what residents then receive.

faq.a: Two verify: Alouette Retirement Mobile Home Park (12868 229 St) and Val Maria (21163 Lougheed Hwy) — both on current listing text that names the park and states the 55+ age restriction.
faq.q: Which Maple Ridge parks are actually 55+?

faq.a: The manufactured home — not the land. You rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, and your purchase is an assignment of that tenancy, which requires the park owner's consent.
faq.q: What do I own when I buy in a 55+ park?

faq.a: In a park whose pads are reserved by age, yes: the MHPTA assignment rules expressly recognise parks reserved for tenants who have reached 55 (Human Rights Code s. 10(2)(b)(i)), and the park owner can refuse an assignment where no purchaser meets the age requirement. The same rule that admits you at 55+ narrows your resale pool the same way a strata bylaw does.
faq.q: Can the park refuse me because of age — or refuse my buyer later?

faq.a: Pad rent is the big one, and it is park-specific: listing-stated figures are $713.31/month at Alouette (plus city taxes of $457.37 and quarterly metered water, per the same listing) and $850/month at Val Maria. Confirm the current figure for the specific pad in the tenancy agreement — pad rent is not a strata fee and is not set by the seller.
faq.q: What are the carrying costs on top of the purchase?

faq.a: It depends on the park — and at Alouette the listing states plainly "no financing permitted in this community." Read the park rules before assuming any lender product applies; a park purchase can be a cash purchase by rule, not just by price.
faq.q: Can I get a mortgage on a park home?

faq.a: Park by park, and opposite at the two parks: Alouette's listing states no dogs, indoor cat only, 2 residents per unit; Val Maria's listing states 2 small pets allowed. Confirm in the park rules for the specific park.

Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street — a Fraser Health community hospital with 24/7 emergency care serving Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows. Both parks are in the urban core's orbit (229 Street east; Lougheed Highway west).

No. A manufactured or modular home on owned land is a freehold purchase — no pad rent, no park rules, no age restriction. The registry covers both forms, which is why they appear on the same page, but the tenure is entirely different.
faq.q: Is a manufactured home on its own lot the same thing as a park home?

faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — a home on a rented pad is not land ownership. Own-land manufactured stock (fee-simple lot, bare-land strata lot, or a co-op share at The Maples) is a different purchase entirely.
faq.q: Do I own the land under a park home?

faq.a: Only as each park's own documents state it. Get the specific park's written rules.

The sale is only effective once registered in the Manufactured Home Registry, and a home may not be sold unless its original legible CSA decal is attached (Z-240 mobile / A-277 modular); a lost label means Technical Safety BC re-certification before sale.
faq.q: Why does the CSA label matter?

faq.a: You get two layers of protection, one provincial and one from the City. The MHPTA sets the legal notice and compensation floor, and the City's Policy No. 6.27 adds communication with residents, relocation planning, financial compensation, moving help, a right to return when possible, and replacement-housing support where a development application would displace residents.
faq.q: What happens to me if my Maple Ridge park is redeveloped?

faq.a: The owner can require consent, but cannot simply ignore the request.
faq.q: Can the park owner block my purchase of a home on a pad?

faq.a: Only by a percentage set by the Province, never by an amount the park chooses freely.
faq.q: How much can my pad rent go up each year?

faq.a: Yes, the same flood rules apply to manufactured homes as to other houses. The City's Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 8121-2026 counts manufactured home pads as structures and requires manufactured homes to meet the same Flood Construction Level as other residential uses, although replacing an existing home in an existing park below that level may be permitted if the non-conformity is not increased and no units are added.
faq.q: Does a manufactured home here have to meet flood construction rules?

faq.a: Both are manufactured homes built off-site. The Province's registry distinguishes them by their CSA standard: mobile homes are built under the Z-240 standards and modular homes under the A-277 standards, and the CSA label on the home states which applies.
faq.q: What is the difference between a mobile home and a modular home in BC?

faq.a: In a manufactured home park, generally no: the Province describes park tenancies as owning the manufactured home and renting the site it sits on, under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act; the home's assessed value for tax purposes does not include the land value in a park.
faq.q: Do I own the land under a Maple Ridge park home?

faq.a: No — on assignment of the site tenancy the pad rental for the new tenant stays the same, and the scheduled date for a subsequent rent increase does not change; increases otherwise require 3 full months' notice, at most once every 12 months, within the yearly limit plus the proportional levy and utility amount.
faq.q: Can the park raise my pad rent when I buy?
